q: 1. The property of fresh concrete, in which the water in the mix tends to rise to the surface while placing and compacting, is called ...........
explain: Bleeding is a form of segregation where water comes out to the surface of the concrete because it has the lowest specific gravity among the ingredients.

q: 2. Workability of concrete is directly proportional to ...........
explain: Better grading of aggregate reduces voids and internal friction, thereby increasing the workability of the concrete mix.

q: 3. Workability of concrete is inversely proportional to ...........
explain: As the time of transit increases, concrete loses moisture due to evaporation and hydration, causing workability to decrease.

q: 4. Approximate value of shrinkage strain in concrete, is ...........
explain: In the absence of specific data, the design value for total shrinkage strain is taken as 0.0003 as per IS:456.

q: 5. Air entrainment in the concrete increases ...........
explain: Air entraining agents create minute air bubbles that act like ball bearings, significantly increasing the workability of the mix.

q: 6. The relation between modulus of rupture fcr, splitting strength fcs and direct tensile strength ft is given by ...........
explain: The modulus of rupture (flexural strength) is always highest, followed by splitting tensile strength, with direct tensile strength being the lowest.

q: 7. Strength of concrete increases with ...........
explain: Finer cement provides more surface area for hydration, leading to a more rapid development of strength.

q: 8. The relation between modulus of rupture fcr and characteristic strength of concrete fck is given by ...........
explain: As per IS:456, the flexural strength of concrete is calculated using the formula 0.7 * sqrt(fck).

q: 9. The compressive strength of 100 mm cube as compared to 150 mm cube is always ...........
explain: Smaller specimen sizes usually exhibit higher apparent compressive strength because of reduced probability of critical flaws and different end-restraint effects.

q: 10. According to I.S.: 456-1978, the modulus of elasticity of concrete Ec (in N/mm2) can be taken as ...........
explain: The older version of the code (IS 456:1978) specified 5700 * sqrt(fck); note that the 2000 version uses 5000 * sqrt(fck).

q: 11. Increase in the moisture content in concrete ...........
explain: Higher moisture content beyond the required water-cement ratio increases the volume of voids once evaporated, thus reducing strength.

q: 12. Admixtures which cause early setting, and hardening of concrete are called ...........
explain: Accelerators are chemicals that speed up the chemical reaction of cement with water, reducing setting time and increasing early strength.

q: 13. The most commonly use admixture which prolongs the setting and hardening time is ...........
explain: Gypsum is added during cement manufacturing to act as a retarder, preventing the 'flash set' of C3A.

q: 14. The strength of concrete after one year as compared to 28 days strength is about ...........
explain: Concrete continues to gain strength over time due to slow hydration; after one year, it is typically 20-25% stronger than at 28 days.

q: 15. As compared to ordinary portland cement, high alumina cement has ...........
options: higher initial setting time but lower final setting time
lower initial setting time but higher final setting time
higher initial and final setting times
lower initial and final setting times
explain: High Alumina Cement (HAC) is characterized by a high initial setting time but a very rapid final setting and hardening process.

q: 16. In reinforced cement concrete structures, the steel reinforcement consists of ...........
options: mild steel and medium tensile steel bars
explain: Reinforced concrete can utilize various types of steel reinforcement including mild steel, CTD, and modern TMT (deformed) bars.

q: 17. A twisted bar has about ........... more yield stress than ordinary mild steel bar.
explain: Cold twisting increases the yield strength of the steel by approximately 50% due to the strain hardening effect.

q: 18. In the limit state method, the compressive force in concrete is taken to act at a distance of ...... times the neutral axis measured from the extreme compression fibre.
explain: Based on the parabolic-rectangular stress block used in IS:456, the centroid of the compressive force is 0.42 times the depth of the neutral axis (xu).

q: 19. The surface width of cracks shall not generally exceed ...........
explain: For members under moderate exposure conditions, the maximum crack width is limited to 0.3 mm to ensure durability.

q: 20. As per I.S.: 456-1978, the pH value of water shall be ...........
explain: Water used for mixing and curing concrete must be clean and have a pH value not less than 6 to avoid acidic attack on the concrete.

q: 21. The increase in strength of concrete after six months is generally ...........
explain: Over a six-month period, the continuous hydration of cement typically adds about 20% to the 28-day strength.

q: 22. Modular ratio in reinforced concrete is defined as ...........
options: Modulus of elasticity of steel / Modulus of elasticity of concrete
Modulus of elasticity of concrete / Modulus of elasticity of steel
Coefficient of linear expansion steel / Coefficient of linear expansion of concrete
explain: Modular ratio (m) is the ratio of the Modulus of Elasticity of Steel (Es) to the Modulus of Elasticity of Concrete (Ec).

q: 23. Working loads may be defined as ...........
options: maximum loads consisting of dead and live loads
a set of critical loads in service conditions
all loads that occur during service conditions
a set of maximum loads for which no failure will occur
explain: Working loads (service loads) are the actual loads expected to occur on the structure during its normal life.

q: 24. The decrease in stress caused in a pre-stressed beam at constant strain is called ...........
explain: Relaxation is the time-dependent decrease of stress in steel held at a constant strain.

q: 25. M 10 grade of concrete approximates ...........
explain: Standard nominal mix proportions for M10 concrete is 1 part cement, 3 parts fine aggregate, and 6 parts coarse aggregate.

q: 26. M 15 grade of concrete approximates ...........
explain: M15 concrete is typically mixed in the ratio of 1:2:4 (Cement:Sand:Aggregate).

q: 27. M 20 grade of concrete approximates ...........
explain: The nominal mix for M20 concrete is 1:1.5:3, providing a characteristic strength of 20 N/mm².

q: 28. M 25 grade of concrete approximates ...........
explain: For M25, the nominal mix is approximately 1:1:2, though higher grades usually require design mixes.

q: 29. The maintenance cost of concrete structures is ...........
options: as much as for timber structures
explain: Unlike steel or timber, concrete does not rust or rot easily, making its long-term maintenance costs very low.

q: 30. The reason for choosing mild steel bars as reinforcement in tensile zones of concrete is that ...........
options: The modulus of elasticity of mild steel is about the same as that of concrete
The Poisson's ratio of mild steel is almost the same as that of concrete
The coefficient of linear expansion is about the same as that of concrete
The stress-strain plots of both mild steel and concrete are identical in shape
explain: Steel and concrete expand and contract at nearly the same rate with temperature changes, preventing internal bond failure.

q: 31. The advantage of concrete is that ...........
options: it can be moulded into any shape and size
it is durable and maintenance cost is practically nil
explain: Concrete is versatile, durable, and naturally fire-resistant, offering all these structural benefits.

q: 32. The probability that the actual strength of the material is more than its characteristic strength is ...........
explain: Characteristic strength is defined as the value below which not more than 5% of test results are expected to fall, meaning 95% are above it.

q: 33. In the limit state design, the strength of concrete as well as the strength of steel is taken to be a random variable that follows ...........
explain: Structural engineering codes assume a Normal (Gaussian) distribution for the frequency of material strength results.

q: 34. The chances for the actual strength of concrete to be less than its characteristic strength are ...........
explain: By definition, the characteristic strength (fck) allows for a 5% probability of failure (strength being lower than fck).

q: 35. The modulus of elasticity of steel is generally taken as ...........
explain: The standard value for the modulus of elasticity of all types of reinforcing steel is 200 kN/mm² or 200,000 N/mm².

q: 36. The design load obtained after multiplying the characteristic load by the partial safety factor is also known as ...........
explain: In Limit State Design, the design load is the factored load (Characteristic Load x γf).

q: 37. In terms of the mean load Fm and the standard deviation of the load Fs, the characteristic load Fk is given by ...........
explain: Characteristic load is the value that has a 95% probability of not being exceeded during the life of the structure.

q: 38. In the limit state method, the maximum strain in concrete in bending compression is taken to be ...........
explain: IS:456 specifies that the maximum compressive strain in the outermost fiber of concrete in bending is 0.0035.

q: 39. The design strength of the materials in the limit state method is given by ...........
explain: Design strength = Characteristic Strength (f) divided by Partial Safety Factor (γm).

q: 40. In limit state design, the relationship between stress strain distribution in concrete is assumed to be ...........
explain: IS:456 assumes a stress-strain curve for concrete that is parabolic up to 0.002 strain and constant thereafter up to 0.0035 strain.

q: 41. Concrete fails at a strain of ...........
explain: In the Limit State of collapse (flexure), the maximum strain in concrete at the outermost compression fiber is assumed to be 0.0035.

q: 42. The shape of the stress-strain curve of concrete up to a strain of 0.002 is ...........
explain: The idealized stress-strain curve for concrete consists of a parabolic portion from zero strain to 0.002, followed by a rectangular portion up to 0.0035.

q: 43. The shape stress-strain curve of mild steel up to yield stress is ...........
explain: Mild steel is a linearly elastic material up to its yield point, meaning stress is directly proportional to strain.

q: 44. In the case of Fe 415 and Fe 500 steels, the yield stress is taken as ....... percent proof stress.
explain: High-strength steels do not have a well-defined yield point, so the yield stress is taken as the stress corresponding to a 0.2% permanent (offset) strain.

q: 45. The moment of resistance factor Ru is given as ...........
explain: The Moment of Resistance (Mu) is calculated as $M_u = R_u \cdot b \cdot d^2$, making $R_u = M_u / (b \cdot d^2)$.

q: 46. Over reinforced section is not desirable because ...........
options: failure is sudden as concrete fails first
explain: In over-reinforced sections, concrete reaches its failure strain before the steel yields, leading to a brittle, explosive failure without warning.

q: 47. The balanced design gives ...........
explain: A balanced section utilizes the full capacity of both materials simultaneously, resulting in the most compact concrete section for a given set of materials.

q: 48. For a fixed beam of span l carrying uniformly distributed load the bending moment at the critical section is given by ...........
explain: For a fixed-ended beam with UDL, the maximum bending moment occurs at the supports (fixed ends) and is equal to $wl^2/12$.

q: 49. The moment of resistance factor Ru, lim when Fe415 steel is used, is given by ...........
explain: For Fe415 steel, the limiting moment of resistance factor is $0.138 \cdot f_{ck}$ based on the strain limit in steel.

q: 50. Which of the following is not a measure adopted for reducing deflection?
explain: Decreasing reinforcement would actually increase deflection; to reduce it, one should increase stiffness (depth or concrete grade) or use camber.
